column1: Would you like to own a robot that did most of the housework?
column2: Yes, definitely. I’m usually very busy with my work and studies everyday. When I come home from work, I am often tired and have no energy left to do household chores. Moreover, my mother is getting older, so a cleaning robot would help reduce her workload at home. As a big fan of technology, having a smart robot in my house is also a dream I have had since childhood.

column1: What laws do you think could change in the future?
column2: I think the law on compulsory military service might change in the future. As an engineering student, I have to spend five years studying hard to get my degree. If graduates must join the army for two years, they might forget their technical skills and fall behind in their careers. Instead of traditional military training, I believe technical graduates should have other ways to contribute, such as working on national technology projects.

column1: What’s your favourite spot in your home?
column2: My favorite spot in my house is definitely my bedroom. It is quite simple with just a bed, a study desk, and a wardrobe, which fits my minimalist lifestyle. The room is very quiet, so it helps me focus well on my work and studies. When I want to relax, I can listen to some light music or look out the window at my mother's flower garden. Seeing the green plants and bright sunlight always makes me feel peaceful.

column1: Who is the most famous person you've met or seen?
column2: The most famous person I have ever seen in person is Son Tung M-TP. If I am not mistaken, I saw him around 2012 at a popular restaurant near my house. This restaurant is a familiar place where many celebrities come to eat when they perform in Da Nang. He was not very tall, but he looked very stylish. Today, he is widely regarded as the top V-pop singer with hits that attract listeners worldwide. I am a huge fan of his music and listen to his songs almost every day.

column1: When you eat in a restaurant do you order something new or something you know you like?
column2: When I eat out, it really depends on who I go with. If I go with my family, I often try new dishes because I love new experiences and usually ask the staff for the best sellers. However, when I eat with colleagues or people I don't know well, I prefer ordering familiar dishes. That way, I can play it safe and avoid dishes that might not suit my taste

column1: Have you ever been bitten or stung by an animal?
column2: No, I have never been bitten or stung by any animal. My family raises a dog at home, and my neighbors have pets too, but they are all very friendly and well-trained."Besides, I live in the city, so I rarely get bitten by dangerous insects or wild animals. Occasionally, I only get minor mosquito bites during the rainy season, which is totally normal.

column1: Have you ever been bitten or stung by an animal?
column2: No, I have never been bitten or stung by any animal. My family does not raise any pets, and only a few of my neighbors have dogs. However, their dogs are usually tied up all day and never allowed to run freely outside. Whenever I see a dog on the street, I never approach it and just walk past calmly, so I always stay safe. Besides, living in a city means I rarely get bitten by insects.

column1: In your opinion, which are the best and worst newspapers?
column2: To be honest, I rarely read printed newspapers, so I cannot name a specific brand as the best or worst. However, in my opinion, good newspapers are the ones that focus on economics, politics, and technology because they provide accurate and useful information for daily life and work. On the other hand, the worst newspapers are tabloid websites that only write gossip about celebrities and normal people. They often use sensational headlines to attract views and likes for commercial profit. These articles usually spread rumors and waste readers' time without offering any real value.

column1: What do you think is the best age to have children?
column2: In my opinion, the best age really depends on gender. For men, I think around 30 to 35 is the ideal time to start a family. At this age, they usually have stable finances and a steady job to support their kids. Moreover, they are mature enough and have plenty of life experience to teach and raise their children well.

column1: Do you think there are too many cars on the road? What's the solution?
column2: Yes, I definitely think so. Cars appear on the streets at all hours of the day, especially during rush hours, which causes serious traffic jams and air pollution. To solve this problem, the government should invest more in public transport like electric buses or trains. In addition, they need to encourage citizens to travel by public transit more often to reduce personal vehicles on the road.

column1: Where will you be this time tomorrow?
column2: At this time tomorrow, I will probably be at home in my room. I do not have to go to work tomorrow, so I will spend my free time learning and improving my skills. Because my English speaking skill is not very good, I plan to spend about one to one and a half hours practicing speaking with an AI application to become more confident.

column1: Describe an impressive work of art you saw
column2:
Today I want to talk about a famous painting called The Starry Night by Vincent van Gogh.
I first learned about this artist when I was in high school. I saw his painting in an art textbook, and later I searched for more of his pictures on Google. This painting immediately caught my attention because it looked very unique and colorful.
The painting shows a small, quiet village at night under a big sky. The stars and the moon are very bright with yellow and blue colors. There is also a large dark tree in front of the village, which makes the picture look special.
The painter was Vincent van Gogh, a very famous artist from the Netherlands.
I really like this painting because it brings a lot of emotions. Even though the picture does not look like a real photo, the colors make the sky look lively, as if it is moving. Looking at this painting always helps me relax, and I never feel bored of seeing it.

column1: Describe a sportsperson from your country who did well in a sports event
column2:
Today I want to talk about Hoang Xuan Vinh, who is a very famous shooter in Vietnam.
I first learned about him during the 2016 Rio Olympics. He became well-known across the country because he won the first Olympic gold medal in Vietnamese sports history.
In real life, he is a very calm, quiet, and disciplined person. Even after becoming famous, he stays modest and does not show off.
His greatest achievement was winning both a gold and a silver medal in shooting at the Olympics.
I really admire him because of his patience and high concentration. Shooting is very difficult because just a small mistake can make you lose. He stayed calm under great pressure to bring glory to our country. He is a great role model for hard work and discipline.

column1: Have you ever been hypnotised?
column2: No, I have never been hypnotized in real life, but I have heard about hypnosis scams on the news. Scammers often approach people on the street, talk continuously, and use psychological tricks to confuse them. In some cases, they might even use strange scents or chemicals to make victims lose their focus. As a result, the victims unintentionally hand over their money and valuable items to the thieves.

column1: What kind of films don't you like?
column2: To be honest, I really dislike watching long TV drama series. I am usually very busy with my work and technical studies every day, so I do not have enough free time to follow hundreds of episodes. Watching a long series feels quite tiring because the plot often drags on with unnecessary drama. Instead, I prefer watching short movies or tech videos that only take about one or two hours.

column1: What are the most popular TV shows in your country?
column2: One of the most popular TV shows in Vietnam is called Sao Nhap Ngu, or Stars Enlist. It is a famous reality show where celebrities like actors and singers join the army for one week. During the show, they must follow strict military rules, wake up early, and do hard physical training just like real soldiers. Audiences love watching it because it is both funny and inspiring to see famous people overcome tough challenges.

column1: Which celebrities annoy you?
column2: To be honest, the celebrities who annoy me the most are online influencers who create toxic drama just to get views and likes on social media. Nowadays, many famous people do not focus on real talent or high-quality content. Instead, they share fake news, show off their wealth, or advertise cheap, unverified cosmetic and medical products to their young followers. What irritates me even more is that when they make serious mistakes or say offensive things, they never offer a sincere apology to the public. Seeing their exaggerated videos and unnecessary arguments appearing constantly on my news feed feels very annoying and tiring. Therefore, I usually click the unfollow or block button immediately to keep my social media experience clean and positive.

column1: What's the longest journey you've ever been on?
column2: The longest journey I have ever taken was a sleeper bus trip from my hometown all the way down to Ho Chi Minh City, which took nearly twenty hours on the road. I went on this trip during a summer vacation with two close friends because we want to save money instead of booking expensive flight tickets. At the beginning of the journey, we felt very excited, chatting happily and looking at the different landscapes through the large windows. However, after sitting and lying down in a cramped bus space for more than ten hours, my back and legs started to ache terribly. The bus made several short stops at highway rest areas so passengers could eat meals and use the restroom, but it was still exhausting because the bumpy road made it difficult to sleep. Although I arrived at my destination with very low energy, reaching the city after such a long journey was truly an unforgettable experience.

column1: Have you seen any famous works of art?
column2: No, I have not had the opportunity to visit world-famous art museums abroad like the Louvre to see legendary masterpieces in person, but I have admired many iconic artworks through high-definition digital collections on the internet. For example, I have spent a lot of time looking at detailed pictures of The Starry Night by Vincent van Gogh and Leonardo da Vinci’s Mona Lisa. I find the rich brushstrokes, colors, and emotional stories behind those classic paintings extremely fascinating. In addition, when I visited a local cultural museum in Hue, I saw traditional lacquer paintings and fine royal embroidery created by skilled Vietnamese artisans. Even though they may not be internationally famous worldwide, seeing those intricate artworks up close made me appreciate the patience and talent of traditional artists very much.

column1: What tips would you give holidaymakers who came to visit your town?
column2: If tourists are planning to visit my hometown Da Nang, I have several useful tips to help them have a great trip. First of all, the best time to visit is between March and August when the weather is warm and sunny, which is perfect for swimming at My Khe Beach and taking outdoor photos. Second, instead of taking expensive taxis every day, visitors should rent a scooter because it is cheap, convenient, and allows them to explore coastal roads and the Son Tra Peninsula at their own pace. Furthermore, travelers must definitely sample local street foods, such as Mi Quang and fresh seafood at night markets, but they should ask for the prices first to avoid being overcharged. Lastly, visitors should go to the Dragon Bride on Saturday or Sunday evening to watch it breathe fire and water, which is a lively and memorable local attraction.

column1: Do you ever get annoyed with yourself? - Có bao giờ bạn cảm thấy khó chịu với chính mình không?
column2: Yes, I definitely get annoyed with myself from time to time, especially when I procrastinate and waste too much time on my phone. Sometimes, I plan to finish a study task or write code early in the evening, but then I get distracted by watching videos or browsing social media for hours. When midnight comes and my work is still not done, I feel really disappointed and angry with my lack of discipline. Another situation is when I make silly, careless mistakes on tests or daily tasks because I rushed through them without double-checking. Whenever that happens, I take a deep breath, write down a clear checklist for the next day, and try to manage my time better so I do not repeat the same mistakes.

column1: How often do you get your hair cut?
column2: I usually get a haircut about once a month or every five weeks. Because I live in a coastal city with hot and humid weather for most of the year, having long hair makes me feel quite uncomfortable and sweaty, especially when I ride a motorbike and wear a helmet. For that reason, I always prefer keeping my hair short, tidy, and neat. I have a regular local barbershop near my house where the barber knows my favorite style, which is a simple short fade on the sides. It only takes about twenty minutes and costs very little money, so going there once a month has become a comfortable routine to keep myself looking fresh and well-groomed.

column1: How do you get your news?
column2: Nowadays, I get almost all of my daily news online through social media platforms and reliable news applications on my smartphone. Instead of reading traditional printed newspapers or waiting for evening television broadcasts like older generations do, I prefer reading digital articles because they are updated every single minute. Every morning while having coffee, I spend about fifteen to twenty minutes browsing through technology websites and local news channels to catch up on what is happening in my country and around the world. However, because there is a lot of fake information on the internet today, I always try to verify hot stories by checking official newspapers before believing them or sharing them with my friends.

column1: Have you ever suffered from buyer’s remorse? - Bạn đã bao giờ cảm thấy hối hận sau khi mua một món đồ nào đó chưa?
column2: Yes, I have experienced buyer's remorse a few times, and the most memorable one was when I bought an expensive mechanical keyboard online about a year ago. At that time, I saw many flashy advertisements and tech reviews praising its colorful lights and satisfying typing sounds, so I made an impulsive decision to order it without thinking carefully. However, when the package arrived and I started using it at home, the clicking sound was so loud that it annoyed everyone around me, especially late at night. On top of that, it did not feel as comfortable for daily typing as my old, cheaper keyboard. I felt very guilty and regretful for wasting a big part of my monthly savings on an unnecessary item, and that experience taught me to always wait a few days before buying expensive gadgets.

column1: What were you afraid of when you were a child?
column2: When I was a little child, my biggest fear was the dark, especially being left alone in a quiet room at night. Back then, I watched several scary ghost movies and listened to folklore stories told by older kids in my neighborhood, so my imagination was very wild. Whenever the bedroom lights were turned off, I used to imagine monsters hiding under my bed or inside the wooden wardrobe, and even the simple shadow of a tree branch on the window looked terrifying to me. Because of that fear, I always needed to sleep with a small nightlight on and covered myself completely with a thick blanket, even during warm nights. As I grew older and learned more about science and reality, I gradually realized there was nothing to fear, and that childhood phobia disappeared completely.
